chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, from Jameel who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a woman entered upon him and mentioned that she had left her son, having placed a quilt over his face, saying he was dead. He said to her: 'Perhaps he did not die. So arise and go to your house, perform ghusl, pray two Rak'at, supplicate, and say: O the One Who endowed him to me when there was nothing, renew His endowment to me.' Then move him, and do not inform anyone of that.' She said: 'So I did it, and moved him, and behold, he was crying.'
ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for reviving a seemingly dead person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the concept of 'sudden death' (al-wafah al-faj'ah) in Shia tradition, where a person appears dead but is merely in a state of suspended animation or deep sleep. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes a specific ritual of purification, two units of prayer, and a supplication invoking God as the Bestower of gifts, highlighting the interplay between divine will and prophetic practice in restoring life. The narrative serves as a practical precedent for using prayer and supplication to discern and reverse apparent death, a key theme in the chapter on Salāt for needs.
